angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 813,969 km at 103.44 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.6674 +/- 0.0106 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 103.44 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.17 +/- 0.11 solar radii from Pidhorodetska et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1437 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..135P/abstract): 813,969 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.1 +/- 0.1 solar masses from Pidhorodetska et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1437 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..135P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6008 +/- 113 K from Pidhorodetska et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1437 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..135P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Pidhorodetska et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1437 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..135P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1437.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.343, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
